117642.name: Chabad House Lubavitch of Eastern Michigan
117642.note: Dec 2022: 'Thirty-seven years ago, Rabbi Yisroel Weingarten and his wife, Shainie, moved from Brooklyn to meet the needs of the Flint Jewish community' (Detroit Jewish News) -> 1985. Checked: not in Chabad's Michigan listings of 1980-81; 'Chabad House of Eastern Michigan' first appears in Dec 1986 - fits 1985. Checked (Nov 7): Michigan Jewish History, Fall 2012 (Jewish Historical Society of Michigan): 'Rabbi Yisroel Weingarten and his wife Shainie Chana established the Chabad House of Eastern Michigan in 1987', in its 25th year. The year kept is their arrival (1985, 'thirty-seven years ago' in Dec 2022); the Chabad House as such is 1987. Medium. Where it was: the Jewish News lists 'Chabad House of Eastern Michigan, 5944 Oak Tree Drive, Flint, Michigan 48504 ... Rabbi Yisrael Weingarten' (Dec 14 1990; also May 15 1987); now 5385 Calkins Road (already in lubavitch.com's directory, Dec 2009).

earlier.where: 5944 Oak Tree Drive, Flint (Jewish News listings, May 1987 and Dec 1990)

118632.name: Chabad House of Western Michigan
118632.note: Detroit Jewish News, 9 Sept 1977: 'Grand Rapids Site of Second Chabad House Student Unit' - Chabad-Lubavitch of Michigan announces the opening of a new Chabad House in Grand Rapids, director Rabbi Yosef Weingarten of Brooklyn. (Corrected: the first pass had 'about 1979', counted back from 'about nine years ago' in 1988.) Where it has been (Jewish News): Sept 9 1977, 'The center is located at 1549 Michigan, near Plymouth Road, in the city's north-east section'; Dec 21 1979, 'New Chabad House Opens. Lubavitch has announced the opening of the Grand Rapids Chabad House, located at 1910 Michigan Ave. N.E.'; now 2615 Michigan Street NE, the Arlene and Rose Lando Center, already listed there in the Jewish News of Feb 22 1991 (https://digital.bentley.umich.edu/djnews/djn.1991.02.22.001/30).

earlier.where: 1549 Michigan Ave. NE, near Plymouth Road, its first Chabad House
1910 Michigan Ave. NE (the new Grand Rapids Chabad House, opened Dec 1979), before the Arlene and Rose Lando Center at 2615 Michigan Ave. NE (there by Feb 1991)

117641.name: Chabad House of Farmington Hills
117641.note: Detroit Jewish News, Nov 24 1972: 'A proud new addition to the multivarious activities of Merkos, BAIS CHABAD is a contemporary Hassidic synagogue and student center in Farmington Township. Housed in a beautiful new building at 28555 Middlebelt Road ... Rabbi Yitschak Kagan heads Bais Chabad together with Rabbi I. M. Lipszyc ... another link in the new network of 71 Lubavitch institutions' the Rebbe asked for in his 71st year; its High Holiday services were there in Aug 1972. It was 'Cong. Bais Chabad of Farmington, Rabbi Y.M. Kagan' in May 1976, and by April 1978 Rabbi Chaim M. Bergstein was 'director of Cong. Bais Chabad of Farmington Hills' (the Bergsteins 'since 1977', Jewish News 2023). So 1972 (corrected from 1977, the Bergsteins' start, after the archive was read again on Nov 7). Where it has been: 28555 Middlebelt Rd. from 1972 (still its address in a Sept 1982 ad); Shabbat services at the Bergsteins' home, 32276 Tareyton, in 1978-81, with High Holidays at 28555 Middlebelt; now 32000 Middlebelt Rd., where lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Dec 28 2009 already lists it (Rabbi Chaim Bergstein), and the Jewish News already lists 'Martha Goldman Center, 32000 Middlebelt Road, Farmington Hills ... Rabbi Chayim M. Bergstein' on Feb 22 1991 (https://digital.bentley.umich.edu/djnews/djn.1991.02.22.001/30), so it moved there between 1982 and 1991.

earlier.where: 28555 Middlebelt Rd. (the Labor Zionist Institute building, later the Lubavitch Educational Center)
Shabbat services at the Bergsteins' home, 32276 Tareyton
